open_issues: SITE vs IRS (phase-out rounding): live noovertimetax.com calculator (/_astro/Calculator.DnjnmUK4.js) uses Math.ceil(excess/1000) x $100 for overtime and tips; Schedule 1-A 2025 lines 11/19 and 2026 draft lines 13/25 round DOWN. Site over-reduces by $100 for any MAGI not on an exact $1,000 step (e.g. single MAGI $150,001: site $100 off, IRS $0). The server follows irs.gov. The read-only local source ~/satellite-repos/examnoovertimetax-site uses floor (correct) but is not what is live.

SITE vs IRS (2026 head-of-household brackets): live site uses 17,600 / 67,100 / 105,700 / 201,775 / 256,200 / 639,000; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 Table 2 says 17,700 / 67,450 / 105,700 / 201,750 / 256,200 / 640,600. The server follows irs.gov.

SITE vs IRS (senior deduction, joint, both 65+): live site caps $12,000 and applies one 6% reduction to the combined amount; Schedule 1-A lines 35-37 (2025) apply the reduction to each spouse's $6,000. Example MAGI $160,000 MFJ both 65+: site $11,400, IRS $10,800. The server follows irs.gov.
Live site offers only single / married / head of household; no married-filing-separately option or message that MFS is excluded.

2027 and 2028 bracket tables and standard deductions were not yet published on irs.gov on 2026-10-30; estimate_tax_savings uses the 2026 tables for those years and returns brackets_are_estimate: true. Update when the 2027 Rev. Proc. is released.
Senior age cutoff for 2027/2028 (born before Jan 2, 1963 / 1964) is extrapolated from the 2025 form and 2026 draft rule, not from a published 2027 form.
Glama listing not submitted (glama.json is in the repo; Glama indexing is outside this brief).
Raw live responses are embedded in this file under live_raw_responses; temp dirs were deleted.

Deduction for 2026: $5,000. Only the FLSA premium (the "half" in time-and-a-half) qualifies, not the straight-time part or any extra premium.

This is an estimate, not tax advice. Check the IRS instructions for Schedule 1-A or ask a tax professional before you file.

content.text:
For tax years 2025-2028, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act lets eligible people deduct qualified overtime premium (up to $12,500, or $25,000 joint), qualified tips (up to $25,000 per return) and an extra $6,000 per person age 65 or older, whether or not they itemize. Married filing separately cannot claim any of them, and each person must have an SSN valid for employment. From 2026, overtime counts only if the employer reports it on Form W-2 box 12 code TT (tips: code TP). Social security and Medicare tax still apply.

This is an estimate, not tax advice. Check the IRS instructions for Schedule 1-A or ask a tax professional before you file.

common_rules.itemizing: Available whether you take the standard deduction or itemize. Claimed on Schedule 1-A; the total goes to Form 1040 line 13b (2025) or line 13a (2026 draft).

overtime.what_qualifies: Only the premium the FLSA requires: one-half of the regular rate for each hour over 40 in a workweek. The straight-time part of overtime pay does not qualify. overtime.limits: Cap $12,500 per return ($25,000 joint, a combined limit, not per spouse). Reduced by $100 for each full $1,000 of MAGI over $150,000 ($300,000 joint).

tools.name: calculate_overtime_deduction
tools.title: No Tax on Overtime deduction
tools.description: Calculates the 2025-2028 federal deduction for qualified overtime pay under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21, IRC 225) as IRS Schedule 1-A Part III does: the $12,500 cap ($25,000 joint), then $100 off per full $1,000 of MAGI over $150,000 ($300,000 joint). Only the FLSA half-time premium qualifies, so it converts hourly rate, overtime hours and multiplier (or total overtime pay) to the qualified amount; double time does not double it. Married filing separately gets $0. Figures copied from irs.gov in Oct 2026.

filing_status.description: Federal filing status. married_filing_separately cannot claim these deductions.

magi.description: Modified adjusted gross income in USD: Form 1040 line 11b plus excluded Puerto Rico and foreign income (Schedule 1-A Part I).

tax_year.description: Tax year, 2025 to 2028. The deductions end after 2028.

qualified_overtime_premium.description: Qualified overtime compensation already known, e.g. Form W-2 box 12 code TT. Use this OR the hourly fields OR total_overtime_pay.

hourly_rate.description: FLSA regular rate of pay per hour, in USD.

overtime_hours.description: Overtime hours over 40 in a workweek, summed for the year.

total_overtime_pay.description: Total pay for the overtime hours (straight time plus premium).

multiplier.description: Overtime pay multiplier. 1.5 = time-and-a-half (default), 2 = double time.

tools.name: calculate_tips_deduction
tools.title: No Tax on Tips deduction
tools.description: Calculates the 2025-2028 federal deduction for qualified tips under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21, IRC 224) as IRS Schedule 1-A Part II does: a $25,000 cap per return for every filing status, then $100 off per full $1,000 of MAGI over $150,000 ($300,000 joint). Self-employed tips count only up to that business's net income. Married filing separately gets $0. Figures copied from irs.gov in Oct 2026.

filing_status.description: Federal filing status. married_filing_separately cannot claim these deductions.

magi.description: Modified adjusted gross income in USD: Form 1040 line 11b plus excluded Puerto Rico and foreign income (Schedule 1-A Part I).

tax_year.description: Tax year, 2025 to 2028. The deductions end after 2028.

employee_tips.description: Qualified tips received as an employee (2025: Form W-2 box 7 or Form 4137; 2026+: W-2 box 12 code TP).

self_employed_tips.description: Qualified tips received in your own trade or business (Form 1099-NEC, 1099-MISC or 1099-K).

self_employed_net_income.description: Net income of the trade or business where the self-employed tips were earned.

tools.name: calculate_senior_deduction
tools.title: Enhanced deduction for seniors (65+)
tools.description: Calculates the 2025-2028 enhanced deduction for seniors under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (P.L. 119-21) as IRS Schedule 1-A Part V does: $6,000 per person age 65 or older by Dec 31, each reduced by 6% of MAGI over $75,000 ($150,000 joint). On a joint return the reduction applies to each spouse's $6,000. Married filing separately gets $0. Figures copied from irs.gov in Oct 2026.

tools.title: Estimate federal tax saved
tools.description: Estimates the federal income tax saved in 2025-2028 by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act overtime, tips and senior deductions combined. It applies each deduction's cap and phase-out, then runs taxable income through the IRS bracket tables for that year (Rev. Proc. 2024-40 for 2025, Rev. Proc. 2025-32 for 2026) before and after. 2027-2028 brackets are not published yet, so it uses 2026 and says so. Federal income tax only.
